From a8aec14230322ed8f1e8042b6d656c1631d41163 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Ira Weiny <ira.weiny@intel.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Mar 2026 12:33:05 -0600
Subject: [PATCH] nvdimm/bus: Fix potential use after free in asynchronous
 initialization

Dingisoul with KASAN reports a use after free if device_add() fails in
nd_async_device_register().

Commit b6eae0f61db2 ("libnvdimm: Hold reference on parent while
scheduling async init") correctly added a reference on the parent device
to be held until asynchronous initialization was complete.  However, if
device_add() results in an allocation failure the ref count of the
device drops to 0 prior to the parent pointer being accessed.  Thus
resulting in use after free.

The bug bot AI correctly identified the fix.  Save a reference to the
parent pointer to be used to drop the parent reference regardless of the
outcome of device_add().

Reported-by: Dingisoul <dingiso.kernel@gmail.com>
Closes: http://lore.kernel.org/8855544b-be9e-4153-aa55-0bc328b13733@gmail.com
Fixes: b6eae0f61db2 ("libnvdimm: Hold reference on parent while scheduling async init")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Reviewed-by: Dave Jiang <dave.jiang@intel.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260306-fix-uaf-async-init-v1-1-a28fd7526723@intel.com
Signed-off-by: Ira Weiny <ira.weiny@intel.com>

diff --git a/drivers/nvdimm/bus.c b/drivers/nvdimm/bus.c
index bd9621d3f73c..45b7d756e39a 100644
--- a/drivers/nvdimm/bus.c
+++ b/drivers/nvdimm/bus.c
@@ -486,14 +486,15 @@ EXPORT_SYMBOL_GPL(nd_synchronize);
 static void nd_async_device_register(void *d, async_cookie_t cookie)
 {
 	struct device *dev = d;
+	struct device *parent = dev->parent;
 
 	if (device_add(dev) != 0) {
 		dev_err(dev, "%s: failed\n", __func__);
 		put_device(dev);
 	}
 	put_device(dev);
-	if (dev->parent)
-		put_device(dev->parent);
+	if (parent)
+		put_device(parent);
 }
 
 static void nd_async_device_unregister(void *d, async_cookie_t cookie)
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Modifications

The patch modifies the file `drivers/nvdimm/bus.c` to fix a use-after-free bug in the asynchronous device registration function `nd_async_device_register()`.

### Modifications in `drivers/nvdimm/bus.c`

- **Added a local variable** `struct device *parent = dev->parent;` at the beginning of `nd_async_device_register()`. This captures a reference to the parent device pointer *before* any `put_device()` calls can potentially free the device `dev`.

- **Changed the final `put_device()` call**: Instead of accessing `dev->parent` (which may have become a dangling pointer if `dev` was freed by an earlier `put_device(dev)`), the code now uses the saved `parent` variable:
  ```c
  if (parent)
      put_device(parent);
  ```

### Relationship between the Modifications

The change is confined to a single function within one file. The key insight is that `dev->parent` is accessed after `device_add()` may have failed, triggering a `put_device(dev)` that could drop the last reference to `dev` and free it. By saving the parent pointer early, the code ensures that the parent reference is dropped safely regardless of the outcome of `device_add()`, thereby eliminating the use-after-free condition.

Here is the commit message:
nvdimm/bus: Fix potential use after free in asynchronous
 initialization

Dingisoul with KASAN reports a use after free if device_add() fails in
nd_async_device_register().

Commit b6eae0f61db2 ("libnvdimm: Hold reference on parent while
scheduling async init") correctly added a reference on the parent device
to be held until asynchronous initialization was complete.  However, if
device_add() results in an allocation failure the ref count of the
device drops to 0 prior to the parent pointer being accessed.  Thus
resulting in use after free.

The bug bot AI correctly identified the fix.  Save a reference to the
parent pointer to be used to drop the parent reference regardless of the
outcome of device_add().

Reported-by: Dingisoul <dingiso.kernel@gmail.com>
Closes: http://lore.kernel.org/8855544b-be9e-4153-aa55-0bc328b13733@gmail.com
Fixes: b6eae0f61db2 ("libnvdimm: Hold reference on parent while scheduling async init")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Reviewed-by: Dave Jiang <dave.jiang@intel.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260306-fix-uaf-async-init-v1-1-a28fd7526723@intel.com
Signed-off-by: Ira Weiny <ira.weiny@intel.com>

Here is the root cause:
In `nd_async_device_register()`, when `device_add()` fails, the function calls `put_device(dev)` which may drop the last reference and free the `dev` structure. Subsequently, the code accesses `dev->parent` to drop the parent reference, but by that point `dev` may already be freed, causing a use-after-free. The original fix (commit b6eae0f61db2) added a reference on the parent but did not save the parent pointer before the potential free of `dev`.

Here is the patch:
 
 static void nd_async_device_register(void *d, async_cookie_t cookie)
 {
 	struct device *dev = d;
+	struct device *parent = dev->parent;
 
 	if (device_add(dev) != 0) {
 		dev_err(dev, "%s: failed\n", __func__);
 		put_device(dev);
 	}
 	put_device(dev);
-	if (dev->parent)
-		put_device(dev->parent);
+	if (parent)
+		put_device(parent);
 }
